description: Attention allocation (devsim/attention.py): how much of each delivered event a listener attends to. Psychological attention (Kahneman 1973 capacity theory), not transformer attention. Every numeric value is a tunable design guess to be calibrated, not a cited effect size. Each parameter carries an evidence tag ([V] verified source, [D] design default, [U] plausible but unverified shape) explained in docs/attention_evidence.md, and its allowed range or choices.

enabled.note: master switch; false gives every event weight 1 and tier FULL, matching the engine without this module

neutral_tag_weight.note: every tag's weight when no rule tags an event (counted in attention_stats.neutral_tags)

keyword_tag_weight.note: tag weight when one of the tag's keywords occurs in the observation text

affinity_base.note: topic affinity of an agent at the trait midpoint (Kahneman's enduring dispositions)

loadings.note: affinity change per unit of a Big Five domain (0-1) away from 0.5; family, romance and money are flat

topic_rules.note: deterministic keyword rule table (whole lowercase words); replace with event metadata where authored

event_tags.note: tags implied by the event id prefix (the delivery path)

w_topic.note: top-down weight of topic fit; the four w_ weights must sum to 1

w_rel.note: top-down weight of closeness to the speaker (design hypothesis, no verified study)

w_ment.note: top-down weight of the closest person mentioned

w_goal.note: top-down weight of goal match (Kahneman's momentary intentions)

closeness_family.note: closeness of a caregiver, child or biological parent with no recorded closeness above 0

closeness_known.note: closeness of a known person with no recorded closeness above 0

g_sur.note: bottom-up gain on surprise (Corbetta and Shulman: unexpected stimuli capture attention)

threat_base.note: threat gain at zero threat sensitivity; g_threat = clip(threat_base + threat_dial_gain x threat_sensitivity)

threat_dial_gain.note: extra threat gain at full threat sensitivity

B_capture.note: bottom-up drive at or above which the event captures attention

a_capture_floor.note: lowest weight of a captured event

B_wake.note: bottom-up drive that wakes an asleep agent (otherwise capacity is K_sleep)

K_max.note: capacity of a rested, unloaded agent at ideal arousal

lam_load.note: capacity lost at full stream load

n_load_ref.note: number of other open streams that counts as full load

arousal_shape.note: capacity vs arousal: 1 - kappa (arousal - 0.5)^2 (Yerkes-Dodson style, shape unverified) or constant 1

kappa.note: curvature of the inverted U; at most 4 keeps the factor nonnegative

theta.note: sharpness of competition between open streams

u0_dys.note: extra mind-wandering pull at full dysregulation

stream_expiry_minutes.note: a stream not seen for longer is dropped when next read

s_0.note: logistic noise scale (logit units), moment-to-moment variability

s_dys.note: extra noise scale at full dysregulation

a_full.note: weight at or above which an event is FULL

a_gist.note: weight at or above which an event is GIST; must be below a_full

lam0_per_minute.note: base hazard of drifting off within a stream, per simulated minute (converted from the engine's days)

d_drift.note: weight multiplier while drifted, unless captured

gamma_enc.note: encoding weight is a^gamma_enc times the existing weight

gist_stability_factor.note: extra stability multiplier of a GIST trace

felt_ignored.note: phase 4, off by default: a face-to-face speaker who notices low attention lowers their closeness to the listener

notice_gain.note: P(speaker notices) = notice_gain x closeness(speaker, listener) x (1 - a)

ignored_penalty.note: closeness the speaker loses toward the listener each time they feel ignored
